title: Brain Chemistry
subtitle: Messages across microscopic gaps
learningObjectives: Describe synthesis, vesicular release, receptor binding and signal termination in chemical neurotransmission.
Explain why transmitter effects depend on receptor subtype, circuit and timing.
Reject the simplistic “single chemical imbalance” model of psychiatric symptoms.

sections.explainSimply: Neurons often pass messages by releasing chemicals into a tiny gap. The next cell reads the chemical with matching receptors.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Neurotransmission depends on synthesis, vesicular release, receptor binding and signal termination through reuptake, diffusion or enzymatic breakdown.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Calcium influx at the presynaptic terminal triggers SNARE-mediated vesicle fusion. Postsynaptic effects vary by receptor subtype, intracellular signalling and the receiving cell’s current state.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A keycard system: the same messenger can open one door, lock another, or do nothing when the reader is absent.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: “Chemical imbalance” is an inadequate clinical model. Symptoms arise from dynamic circuits, learning, physiology and context—not a single low or high transmitter.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Receptor dysregulation, impaired clearance, medication interactions and substance use can alter signalling across multiple networks.
sections.clinicalPearl: A neurotransmitter has no fixed psychological meaning outside its receptor, circuit, timing and context.
sections.practicalExample: Serotonin can produce different effects in different circuits because receptor families couple to different intracellular pathways and are expressed on different cell types.
sections.limitationsCautions: Neurotransmitter measures at the group level do not diagnose an individual. Psychological symptoms emerge from interacting circuits, development, learning, physiology and context.

quizBank.question: What directly triggers vesicle release at the presynaptic terminal?
quizBank.explanation: Incoming action potentials open voltage-gated calcium channels, initiating vesicle fusion and transmitter release.
